title: Interpret available memory and cache
goal: Distinguish free memory, available memory and cache without manufacturing pressure.
challenge: Retain live memory observations and interpret the supplied synthetic example. Explain why low free memory alone does not establish a shortage, what evidence would strengthen a pressure diagnosis, and why no OOM experiment is appropriate.

steps.explanation: Create a unique private guest workspace. Retain its printed path; repeat starts a new workspace, never overwrites old evidence. Stop if creation/change-directory fails.
steps.expected: A new /home/learner/capacity-memory.XXXXXX directory. All files below are guest-local.

steps.explanation: Inspect real guest counters and their displayed units; /proc meminfo uses KiB despite its kB label.
steps.expected: Values vary; MemAvailable estimates what new applications can use without swapping.

steps.explanation: Observe swap-in/out and context without allocating a pressure workload.
steps.expected: Zero swap or quiet intervals are valid. No swap does not prove unlimited memory.

steps.command: printf '%s\n' 'SYNTHETIC example; MiB, not this VM' 'total=2048 free=120 available=1200 cached=900 swap_total=0' > memory-example.txt
steps.explanation: Create a small teaching case by typing this exact printf.
steps.expected: A manually created scenario, not collected historical evidence.

steps.explanation: Interpret it rather than adding free and cached as an exact available formula.
steps.expected: Low free with substantial available/cache is not sufficient evidence of a shortage.

hints: free is unused memory; available includes an estimate of reclaimable memory.
Look for sustained symptoms and relevant counters, not one alarming number.
Without swap, si/so cannot demonstrate swap activity; use honest limits.
review: I separated live counters from the synthetic case.
I explained cache reclaimability without assuming all cache is instantly reclaimable.
I described missing evidence rather than claiming OOM or exhaustion.
coverage: Partial 200.1 memory interpretation; no pressure generation or full memory troubleshooting. Completion records self-review, not verified guest assessment; there is no score.
